states.name: paragraph
states.gap: Tighter interline gutter in the lit paragraph: A's ascender-to-descender ink band is 41px inside the same 74px line advance, leaving 33px of air between the two lit lines vs B's 38px band leaving 36px — ~9% less breathing room, so the focused block reads as a denser slab; A also wraps one character earlier (62 chars/line vs B's 63) at the same ~1612px column.
states.gapTheirs: The lit text is ~7% smaller at identical ink and identical leading: cap height 28px vs A's 30px, x-height 23px vs 24px, ink band 38px vs 41px, advance 25.6px vs 26.0px — so against the pixel-identical #C6C4C2 dim, B's lit paragraph carries less mass and the lit/dim step announces itself less.
states.verdict: These are near-twins — same #F7F7F7 page, same #191919 lit ink, same #C6C4C2 dim, same 74px advance, same left edge — so the dimming decides nothing here and the lit paragraph decides everything. A sets that paragraph at 30px cap / 24px x-height, B at 28 / 23, in the same 74px box. Write in B for an afternoon and you feel the lit line underperforming: you dimmed the entire page to make one paragraph matter, then set it 7% smaller than the other guy did. A pays for that with a 33px gutter instead of 36px, which is the lesser sin when the dim tier — not the leading — is what isolates the active line.

states.name: dark-sentence-typewriter
states.gap: Leading is 2px tighter per line: caret/line box 74px device (37 CSS, ~1.69 ratio at ~22px type) vs B's 76px (38 CSS, ~1.74). Across a 7-line dimmed paragraph that is 14px less air, and the grey blocks above and below the lit sentence pack correspondingly closer to it.
states.gapTheirs: B renders a third shade the palette does not have: on the boundary line, 'beside it.' is #cccccc, then 'The door took both hands to open.' comes back at #888888 (grey 136, a 3413px flat plateau in the histogram), and only 'Outside, the wind' drops to the real dim #707070. A goes #cccccc straight to #707070 with no intermediate. Second offence: B sets '#'/'##' inline at the body edge (x=622), so heading words start at x=673 and x=698 — 51px and 76px (≈26 and 38 CSS px) right of every body line at x=623; A hangs the marks out to x=571 and x=545 and keeps one flush left spine.
states.verdict: B's focus mode cannot make up its mind what it is dimming: the sentence after your caret is lit at #888888, the one after that at #707070, so the eye lands on a fading band about 1.5 sentences wide instead of on the sentence you are writing. That near tier is exactly the thing you notice at 2am when you are trying to fix one clause — you keep re-reading the door sentence because it is still half-lit and half-asking for attention. A pays for its clean two-step with 2px less leading per line, which is a fair trade and a one-line CSS argument; B's is a wrong idea rendered correctly. B then compounds it by shunting heading words 26–38px right of the body margin while A hangs the hashes and keeps the left edge straight.
